<description>
This PR changes `-acceptnonstdtxn=1` so that it also skips the non-mandatory script checks, allowing txs that (eg) use OP_NOPx or OP_SUCCESS into the mempool. This remains only available on test nets.
</description>

[2026-09-22] rc:4067643100 inline on src/validation.cpp by ajtowns (member) (edited 2026-09-24):
I don't think restricting the structure of `GetBlockScriptFlags` like that is a good idea; you can see the knots [BIP110/RDTS deployment logic](https://github.com/bitcoinknots/bitcoin/blob/58398baf33e588779685ead478e6397bb28ed3d6/src/validation.cpp#L2756-L2761) for one (not necessarily very good) example where that structure was diverged from.

I've bumped the PR with mostly the same logic but defining a `ConsensusScriptVerifyFlags` class instead, which may come across as easier to follow.
[2026-09-23] rc:4085116408 inline on src/validation.cpp by fjahr (member) (edited 2026-09-24):
I would slightly prefer that we clean this up already and remove the unused constants right away instead of leaving them for a follow-up. If they are left for a follow-up it would be nice to have a comment that these are unused and will be removed.

nit: The names of the reported error aren't that interesting to name here IMO. I think something like this would be more helpful:

```
/** Context CheckInputScripts is called in, which decides how a script failure is

 *  the mempool. The flags alone can't tell, as the mempool may check with consensus
 *  flags only (-acceptnonstdtxn). */
```
[2026-09-24] rc:4093958881 inline on src/validation.cpp by fjahr (member) (edited 2026-09-24):
I think it would be better to move this `Assume` into `GetBlockScriptFlags` at the end where you are adding the comment. The comment could even be shortened or removed then, I think. This would be the more natural placement for me.
[2026-09-24] rc:4094107313 inline on src/validation.cpp by fjahr (member) (edited 2026-09-24):
Comment suggestion, maybe even more commentary on the approach would have helped me with the review but I fear such details may go stale or could also be confusing to someone else.

```suggestion
/** Helper class that holds the flags built up by GetBlockScriptFlags() and
 *  GetAllConsensusScriptFlags(). Any flag added there that is not in
 *  CONSENSUS_SCRIPT_VERIFY_FLAGS fails to compile, regardless of the check
 *  that decides whether to add it. A new soft fork can therefore use any
 *  activation logic and its flags are still covered.
 */
```
